- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is positive but recent prices are trending down, model often ignores the trend — increase forecast slope downward to match sentiment decay.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–5 days ahead) — add 1–2% buffer to initial forecast values.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.5 → +0.2), model fails to capture momentum — apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.  
- If true outcome is significantly higher than model (e.g., >+3% over 30d), check if sentiment was bullish in prior 5–7 days — if yes, model may be underweighting sentiment — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- Model often ignores sentiment when price is near support/resistance — if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, forecast should not be below 1–2% below recent low.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean reversion — reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or neutral over last 7 days.
